claims.text: Traditional EAM references cannot adequately represent the diversity of atomic configurations in ab initio liquids of multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
Replacing an EAM reference with an MLIP trained on a broader sample of ab initio liquid configurations will improve reference–target phase-space overlap.
Improved phase-space overlap from the MLIP will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to TOR-TILD's EAM references.
The relevant materials are typically equiatomic or near-equiatomic alloys containing four to five elements.
A neural-network potential or Gaussian approximation potential can be trained on diverse ab initio liquid configurations characteristic of multicomponent, high-melting-point alloys.
The proposed method applies to high-entropy alloys with four to five principal elements at approximately 0.9–1.1 times their melting temperature.
Near the melting temperature, liquid-state complexity limits the representability of simpler potentials such as EAM.
An MLIP provides a more flexible mapping of interatomic forces and energies than the rigid EAM functional form.
This flexibility allows an MLIP to represent a wider diversity of liquid atomic configurations than EAM.
Training on ab initio molecular-dynamics configurations spanning the relevant phase space significantly improves reference–target phase-space overlap.
A reference potential that more closely reproduces the ab initio free-energy landscape produces a smoother and shorter thermodynamic-integration path.
The MLIP reference is predicted to reduce the integration-path mismatch or associated free-energy error by approximately 30–50% relative to TOR-TILD's EAM references.
TOR-TILD's EAM references are adequate for simpler systems but exhibit significant phase-space mismatch for complex liquid multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
The improvement is expected mainly in high-melting-temperature regimes where the liquid has extensive configurational diversity.
The MLIP's advantage may diminish for systems with less configurational complexity or at temperatures well below melting.
Preliminary elemental and binary studies suggest that MLIPs capture more of the liquid configurational spectrum than simpler references.
The quantitative improvement depends on the quality and diversity of the ab initio training data.
